title: settings.json allows `git rebase *` and `git commit *`, so `git rebase --exec` runs any command, push included, and --no-verify skips the commit hooks
goal: .claude/settings.json allows only the rebase and commit forms a headless run needs (`git rebase origin/main`, `--continue`, `--abort`; `git commit` forms without --no-verify) for Bash and PowerShell, and permissions.deny names `git rebase * --exec *`, `git rebase * -x *`, `git commit * --no-verify *` and `git commit --no-verify *` (both shells); test_settings_allow asserts the narrow allows and the denies with a planted failure for each; found by the SP-itmjxudu review: the deny rules match the leading words, so an --exec payload reaches `git push`

run: import json,sys;p=json.load(open(".claude/settings.json"))["permissions"];a=p["allow"];d=p["deny"];bad=[x for x in ("Bash(git rebase *)","Bash(git commit *)") if x in a];need=[n for n in ("--exec","--no-verify") if not any(n in x for x in d)];print(bad,need);sys.exit(1 if bad or need else 0)

repro_reason: a permission decision is made by Claude Code when a tool call is attempted and no repro here can run one; the defect is the allow list, so the repro reads the configuration
